title: Microsoft told Google it was overreacting in 2010. It has spent five years quietly leaving China
excerpt: Microsoft China accounts for 1.5% of revenue and 15+ offices have closed in five years. It weighed quitting in 2023. Azure exports keep it there.
content_html:
Corporate filings show the closures, Reuters reported in an exclusive.

The revenue figure is the one that explains the rest. China accounted for 1.5% of global revenue as of 2024.

Microsoft has no current plan to exit. It has simply stopped growing there.

Put 1.5% against the scale of the company and it almost disappears. Microsoft’s cloud business alone crossed $100bn in annual revenue in its most recent quarter.

China is now a rounding error attached to a large geopolitical risk. That is the calculation every sentence below follows from.

The company that told Google it was overreacting

The history makes this sharper than a normal retreat story. In 2010 Google left China over censorship and cyberattacks.

Bill Gates and Steve Ballmer, then chief executive, suggested Google was overreacting. Microsoft stayed, and democracy activists praised Google for going.

Sixteen years later Microsoft is arriving at the same place slowly, without ever announcing it.

That is the difference worth noticing. Google made a decision. Microsoft has made a series of quiet ones, and the filings are where you find them.

2023 was the year it nearly went

The internal argument got as far as the exit question. Reuters reports that Microsoft weighed quitting China in 2023.

Some executives held that the company took on too much geopolitical risk for too little economic return. Read that sentence next to the 1.5% and it is hard to argue with.

Then came the staff question. In 2024 Microsoft offered 1,000 of its top engineers relocation to the US and three other Western countries.

About a third accepted. Two thirds of the people it most wanted to move chose to stay, which is its own commentary on how these offers land.

The state stopped buying

The commercial squeeze is documented rather than inferred. China has pushed domestic software since 2017.

By May 2026 five of six reviewed Chinese government procurement guides did not recommend Microsoft products. The sixth listed Windows 10 China Government Edition, with additional management requirements attached.

A procurement guide is not a ban. It is more effective than one, because nobody has to defend it.

The pressure runs both ways. China has opened a cybersecurity review into Palo Alto Networks, and Washington has moved to push Chinese optics out of American data centres in a transceiver ban that Microsoft pays for directly.

What actually keeps the window open

Here is the part the headline number hides. Microsoft’s remaining China business is largely about Chinese companies leaving China.

Azure serves firms including ByteDance and Shein, which need Western technology to operate overseas. The customer is Chinese. The workload is not.

That is a durable position, and it is a strange one. Microsoft’s China strategy now depends on Chinese companies expanding abroad rather than on selling into China.

Shein illustrates the fragility. Its advisers are pitching a Hong Kong listing at under $30bn, down sharply from its peak.

Microsoft Research Asia tells the same story in miniature. Its labs now sit in Vancouver, Singapore and Tokyo.

The AI boom is what makes the position worth keeping at all. Companies building for overseas markets need Western models, Western tooling and a cloud their foreign customers already trust.

Without that demand, the argument for staying would rest on 1.5% and a long history. Neither of those wins an internal debate.

Where the money went instead

Follow the capital and the retreat looks less like withdrawal than redirection. Microsoft brought its fourth Indian cloud region online this month, against a $17.5bn commitment.

That is one country receiving a commitment larger than the entire revenue contribution of another. India gets regions and megawatts. China gets a maintained presence.

Microsoft’s own line is diplomatic. A spokesperson said the company operates in a regulatory environment that applies to every international supplier, and remains committed to the Chinese market.

Both halves of that sentence are true. It is also the sort of statement a company issues when the numbers have already spoken.

The technology still flows, in one direction

The relationship has not ended, it has inverted. Microsoft has reportedly considered putting China’s DeepSeek inside Copilot to control its AI costs.

So the American company retreating from the Chinese market is weighing whether to run Chinese models in its flagship product.

That is not a contradiction. It is what decoupling actually looks like from inside a business, where the politics and the bill of materials point in opposite directions.

Why this matters outside China

Europe should read this as a precedent rather than a curiosity. A government that wants domestic software can achieve it through procurement guidance alone, in under a decade, without passing a single ban.

That is the mechanism, and it is available to any state. The EU has spent years debating digital sovereignty in terms of rules and funding.

China did it with purchasing decisions, and the result is a 1.5% revenue line at the world’s largest software company.

The counterargument deserves stating. China’s approach comes bundled with censorship, forced localisation and an industrial policy Europe would not accept, and the outcome is a market Western firms increasingly cannot serve.

What would settle it

Two things are checkable. The first is whether the 1.5% falls further in the next annual disclosure, because a number that small can still halve.

The second is the Azure business specifically. If Chinese companies expanding overseas keep buying Western cloud, Microsoft has a real position rather than a legacy one.

The exit question has an obvious answer that nobody at Microsoft will give. It stayed in 2010 to make a point, considered leaving in 2023 for sound reasons, and remains today because a decision it never announced is easier to live with than one it would have to defend.

content_html_zh:
据路透社独家报道，公司备案文件显示了关闭的情况。

收入数字可以解释其余部分。 截至2024年，中国占全球收入的1.5%。

微软目前没有退出计划。 它只是在那里停止生长了。

如果将 1.5% 与公司规模相比较，它几乎就消失了。 最近一个季度，仅微软云业务的年收入就突破了 1000 亿美元。

中国现在因四舍五入误差附加了很大的地缘政治风险。 这就是下面每个句子的计算结果。

告诉谷歌反应过度的公司

历史使这比正常的撤退故事更加尖锐。 2010年，谷歌因审查制度和网络攻击而离开中国。

比尔·盖茨和时任首席执行官史蒂夫·鲍尔默表示谷歌反应过度。 微软留下来，民主活动人士赞扬谷歌的离开。

十六年后，微软正在慢慢地达到同样的目标，但从未宣布过。

这就是值得注意的差异。 谷歌做出了决定。 微软已经制作了一系列安静的产品，您可以在这些文件中找到它们。

2023 年是它即将过去的一年

内部争论一直延伸到退出问题。 据路透社报道，微软考虑在 2023 年退出中国。

一些高管认为，该公司承担了太多的地缘政治风险，而获得的经济回报却太少。 读一下 1.5% 旁边的那句话，你很难反驳。

接下来是工作人员的问题。 2024 年，微软将 1,000 名顶级工程师调往美国和其他三个西方国家。

大约三分之一被接受。 它最想搬走的人中有三分之二选择留下来，这是它自己对这些报价如何落地的评论。

国家停止购买

商业挤压是有记录的而不是推断的。 中国从2017年开始大力推国产软件。

到 2026 年 5 月，经过审查的六份中国政府采购指南中有五份没有推荐微软产品。 第六个列出的是Windows 10中国政府版，附加了额外的管理要求。

采购指南不是禁令。 它比一个更有效，因为没有人需要捍卫它。

压力是双向的。 中国已对 Palo Alto Networks 展开网络安全审查，华盛顿已采取行动，通过微软直接支付费用的收发器禁令，将中国光学器件逐出美国数据中心。

到底是什么让窗户保持打开状态

这是标题数字隐藏的部分。 微软剩下的中国业务主要是中国企业离开中国。

Azure 为字节跳动和 Shein 等公司提供服务，这些公司需要西方技术才能在海外运营。 顾客是中国人。 工作量则不然。

这是一个持久的立场，也是一个奇怪的立场。 微软的中国战略现在取决于中国公司向海外扩张，而不是向中国销售产品。

谢因说明了脆弱性。 其顾问预计在香港上市的估值将低于 300 亿美元，较峰值大幅下跌。

微软亚洲研究院也讲述了同样的故事。 其实验室目前位于温哥华、新加坡和东京。

人工智能的蓬勃发展使得这个职位值得保留。 面向海外市场的公司需要西方模型、西方工具和外国客户已经信任的云。

如果没有这一要求，留下来的理由将取决于 1.5% 和悠久的历史。 这些都没有赢得内部辩论。

钱去了哪里

追随资本的脚步，撤退看起来不像是撤退，而更像是重新调整方向。 微软本月在印度推出了第四个云区域，承诺投入 175 亿美元。

即一个国家获得的承诺大于另一个国家的全部收入贡献。 印度获得了地区和兆瓦。 中国保持存在。

微软自己的路线是外交的。 一位发言人表示，该公司在适用于所有国际供应商的监管环境中运营，并将继续致力于中国市场。

这句话的两半都是正确的。 这也是公司在数字已经说明一切后发布的声明。

技术仍在朝一个方向流动

关系还没有结束，而是倒转了。 据报道，微软已考虑将中国的 DeepSeek 放入 Copilot 中，以控制其人工智能成本。

因此，这家退出中国市场的美国公司正在考虑是否在其旗舰产品中运行中国车型。

这并不矛盾。 这就是企业内部脱钩的实际情况，其中政治和物料清单指向相反的方向。

为什么这在中国以外很重要

欧洲应该将此视为一个先例，而不是一种好奇心。 想要国产软件的政府可以在不到十年的时间内仅通过采购指导来实现这一目标，而无需通过任何禁令。

这就是机制，任何国家都可以使用。 欧盟多年来一直在规则和资金方面争论数字主权。

中国通过采购决策做到了这一点，其结果是全球最大的软件公司的收入增加了 1.5%。

反驳值得说明。 中国的做法与审查制度、强制本地化和欧洲不会接受的产业政策捆绑在一起，其结果是西方公司越来越无法服务的市场。

什么可以解决它

有两件事是可以检查的。 首先是下一年披露时1.5%是否会进一步下降，因为这么小的数字仍然可以减半。

第二个具体是Azure业务。 如果向海外扩张的中国企业继续购买西方云，那么微软将拥有真正的地位，而不是传统的地位。

对于退出问题，微软没有人会给出一个显而易见的答案。 它在 2010 年留下来是为了表明自己的观点，考虑在 2023 年出于合理的原因退出，并且一直保留到今天，因为它从未宣布的决定比它必须捍卫的决定更容易接受。
